It should be noted that C-14 is a low energy beta emitter. Such radiation cannot penetrate glass, a sheet of paper, or the human skin. In the event of spillage, the total amount of C-14 would be dissipated to non-detectable levels in minutes, therefore there is no radiation hazard to humans or other organisms. Any spillage or unaccounted for materials will be reported to the Radiation Safety Officer at McMurdo.
10. Stack and Exhaust Emissions. Operation of power generating equipment will lead to emission of gases and particulate matter. The gases will be dispersed in the atmosphere and particulate matter will be deposited downwind. Neither of these constitutes a pollution problem. However, geochemists involved in RISP will be consulted routinely on this and other atmospheric fallout problems.
11. <u>Noise and Vibrations</u>. The generating plant and drilling will cause considerable local noise and vibration, but this is a transitory impact on the surface environment which is essentially abiotic. However, it is possible that the drill bit and stem will cause some noise and vibration within the water column and the sediments beneath. These may have minor effects on the biota, if present, and may cause local and temporary disturbance of the soft sediments.
